Done. The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 0 failures/errors).

## What I did

Reject creating an owner when the target city already holds 50+ owners, responding 409 — implemented as small, cohesive new units mirroring the existing household-uniqueness rule, so I didn't grow any existing class:

- **`EnsureCityCapacity`** (new function) — counts owners in the request's city case-insensitively and throws when the count is ≥ 50.
- **`CityAtCapacityException`** (new checked exception) — extends `Exception` so it surfaces on the `throws` clause.
- **`CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler`** (new handler) — responds `409 Conflict`.
- **`...CityAtCapacityException.yml`** (new escalation mapping) — wires the exception to its handler.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** (edited) — inserted the `ensureCityCapacity` step between `ensureUniqueHousehold` and `build`, under the same `transaction` governance.

Structural impact was kept minimal: the only edited existing function is the YAML pipeline wiring (a 4-line insertion); all logic lives in brand-new classes with essentially zero surrounding complexity (`WMC_other ≈ 0`, low CC), rather than being bolted onto an existing method or class.
